key_insight: Critically damped Polyak (CDP) stepsizes steer gradient descent toward flatter minima while enabling convergence through curvature-adaptive steps and damping.
engineering_relevance: CDP offers an adaptive stepsize strategy for reducing solution sharpness, with reported flattening effects in neural networks and pre-trained LLM fine-tuning.
method: Multiply the classical Polyak stepsize by 4 and a mild damping factor.
Use leading-order equioscillations around the minimizer manifold, with damping driving convergence.
At low loss, induce motion along the manifold that reduces log top-Hessian-eigenvalue sharpness.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports uniform-in-time sharpness and loss-reduction guarantees for locally quadratic Morse–Bott losses, plus empirical flattening similar to SAM in nonlinear teacher–student networks and LLM fine-tuning.
watch_item: The theory requires local Morse–Bott structure near the minimizer manifold; empirical success beyond this regime does not establish the same guarantees.
paper_title: A new algorithmic approach for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes
